Thanks Jordan — useful framing. Quick answers below and looping in Victor from procurement for the details.

- Target uptime: aiming for 99.95 for production model endpoints. We understand 99.99 is expensive, but open to the discussion.
- Response windows: Sev1 (production outage impacting >50% of traffic) — 30 minutes to acknowledge and 2 hours to remediation plan; Sev2 — 2 hours to acknowledge; Sev3 — 1 business day.
- Escalation: yes, we need a named escalation contact and a documented on-call handoff for any overnight incidents.
- Procurement constraints: 12–24 month term; we have internal discount target of ~25% off list for renewals at our ARR band; require invoice/PO process, gov billing entity.

Victor — can you add anything on the PO / compliance side?

Samira

Samira, Victor — thanks for the clarity. Looping Neha (your RED account lead) to keep everyone aligned on commercial constraints.

Attached is the pricing worksheet with three options and a short commentary on how we measure uptime and credits. Highlights:
- Core (no guaranteed uptime credit, email-first support, 1 business day response) — baseline price
- Assured (99.95 uptime, 4h Sev1 ack / 12h remediation SLA, named escalation during business hours) — mid-tier price
- Premium (99.99 uptime, 30m Sev1 ack / 2h remediation SLA, 24/7 named escalation + quarterly operational review) — premium price

Given Brightline’s ARR band you mentioned, the incremental cost from Assured -> Premium is significant because of reserved capacity and the 24/7 escalation coverage. However, two ways to get closer to your 25% target:
1) Commit to a 24-month term and we can do step-down pricing in year 2 (10% year 1, +5% year 2) to approach your target.
2) Keep Premium only for the critical production endpoints (you can designate up to 3 endpoints) and keep others on Assured — this hybrid approach preserves incident economics while lowering unit cost.

I also included an addendum explaining our failure-mode fallbacks (model variant routing + cross-region failover) and the credit calculation.

Attachments: SLA_pricing_sheet_Brightline.xlsx, Brightline_SLA_options_2027.pdf

Would you prefer a short call to walk procurement through the worksheet Thursday or Friday?

Best,
Jordan Blake

Subject: Re: SLA & Premium Support — technical notes on failover and scope

Hi all — quick technical note from the Ops side to help with pricing scoping.

Two items that materially affect cost:
1) Reserved capacity sizing: Premium 99.99 requires dedicated reserved GPU capacity sized for your 95th percentile peak. That capacity is billed whether used or not; so whether you choose per-endpoint Premium (hybrid) vs all endpoints matters.
2) Cross-region failover: If you require cross-region automatic failover with guaranteed RTOs, we need to provision cold-warm pools in the failover region — this adds a small fixed monthly fee and a warm-standby weight to the reserved capacity calculation.

Recommendation: For Brightline, designate 2 production endpoints as Premium, keep the rest on Assured, and enable asynchronous cross-region failover (not automatic) for non-Premium endpoints. That preserves 24/7 escalation for the most critical traffic and limits reserved capacity costs.

I’ve also added the operational runbook stub as a page in the attached PDF (see section: On-call handoffs). Happy to jump on the call if you want to run through the runbook.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineering — Customer Reliability

Jordan / Neha — looping back after internal procurement review. We like the Premium/Assured hybrid recommendation but procurement has two asks before we proceed:

1) Pricing: can you provide a final commercial with a 20–25% consolidated discount if we do a 24-month commitment and pay annually? We can push to 25% with an executive approval window.

2) Delivery / liability: we need the uptime credit calculation clarified in the SOW (monthly measurand, rolling 30-day window, cap on credits), and a maximum liability cap equal to 12 months of SLA fees.

We also attached a redline to your SOW (attached to this email in our system) — happy to do a short call Tuesday to resolve redlines. Please advise if these two requests are deal breakers or if you can accept them with the hybrid packaging.

Regards,
Victor Lu
